brief: Security fix SEC-5 (tighten-only). redact.scrub_text applies credential_patterns.PATTERNS, whose private-key entries match only the '-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----' header and the '-----END ...-----' footer, so the base64 body between them goes out unredacted to everything scrub_text feeds (the Discord mirror and reporter, diff review, chat git, providers, subagents, the daemon). Make scrub_text redact a private key's whole block, in jarvis/v2/redact.py, as one [redacted]: a terminated block (header to the nearest private-key footer; two blocks stay two), an unterminated block (header to the end of the text), and a footer-only tail (the key-material lines directly above a lone footer, back to the first line that is not base64, a PGP checksum, or a Proc-Type/DEK-Info line, and no further). Cover RSA, OPENSSH, EC, ENCRYPTED (PKCS#8 and legacy), PGP and plain PKCS#8 blocks. Take the header and footer regexes from credential_patterns.PATTERNS by name rather than copying them. Tighten-only: text with no private-key header or footer must come out byte-identical to today's scrub, and no token the old scrub hid may be shown by the new one (a token-character run glued to the front of a header goes with the block). Public keys and certificates are unchanged. Matching must be linear: 1 MiB adversarial inputs must finish within a CPU bound. Interface the tests call directly: redact.private_key_blocks(text) -> str, which keeps CRs (scrub_text itself normalises line endings via secrets.scrub). Key bodies in tests are random base64 from a seeded RNG, never real keys.
